question: How do combat scheduling, equipment, damage and hit-feedback selection consume shared state?

new_logic.opponent_clock: BYTE decrement; expiry reloads, adds two for reload 1 or one otherwise, then compares charge low BYTE with 23. Attempt clears the charge WORD before the comparand gate.
new_logic.player_clock: Negative overlay flag WORD gates all work. BYTE expiry adds one for reload 1 or two otherwise; updated WORD above 40 clears. Zero countdown wraps.
new_logic.player_fire: Charge low BYTE 0..16 clears, 17..22 selects half damage, 23..24 full damage, 25..255 retains charge. Gauge service follows the decision.
new_logic.damage: Player defeat uses unsigned borrow or equality. Opponent subtraction writes the BYTE first and defeats on negative result or equality; a wrapped positive result can survive.
new_logic.equipment: BYTE IDs 7..13 select seven reload/damage pairs with C=1; fallback uses full MOVEQ 3/5 and C=0. Kriptonite reduction precedes actor-specific overrides.
new_logic.gauge: 24 packed rows by five bytes are cleared. Full cells consume repeated four-byte patterns, followed by a masked partial cell. All 41 normal charge states are memory-compared.

selector_alias.proof: Original builder executes to completion with a stack outside the grid. Both feedback helpers then execute using its selector, and attack-gate values 83/84 take opposite branches. All 4212 original pixel offsets are 128-byte aligned and force feedback indices 2/0.
